parts.text:
2
Which pair of quantities do not have the same SI base units?
A
electromotive force and electric potential difference
B
pressure and stress
C
spring constant and moment of a force
D
torque and work

hints: Notice the word not, so three pairs share identical SI base units and you are looking for the one mismatch in force, length and time powers.
Write each quantity with its defining equation: $F = kx$ for spring constant, moment $= Fd$, pressure $= F/A$, work $= Fs$, and e.m.f. as $W/Q$.
Compare $\text{N m}^{-1}$ against $\text{N m}$: dividing by a metre versus multiplying by a metre cannot give the same $\text{kg}$, $\text{m}$ and $\text{s}$ powers.
walkthrough: Express every quantity in newtons, metres, seconds and other base units. Recall $1 \text{ N} = 1 \text{ kg m s}^{-2}$.
Check electromotive force and potential difference: both are $W/Q$ in volts, giving $\text{kg m}^2 \text{s}^{-3} \text{A}^{-1}$, so they are the same.
Check pressure and stress: both are $F/A$ in $\text{N m}^{-2}$ or pascals, so they are the same.

Check spring constant and moment: from $k = F/x$, $k$ has units $\text{N m}^{-1} = \text{kg s}^{-2}$, while moment $= F \times d$ has units $\text{N m} = \text{kg m}^2 \text{s}^{-2}$, so the power of $\text{m}$ differs.
Check torque and work: torque $= F \times d$ and work $= F \times s$ both give $\text{N m} = \text{kg m}^2 \text{s}^{-2}$, so they are the same despite different physical meanings.
Only the spring constant and moment pair do not match. This is option C.

A.explanation: Both are energy per unit charge in volts, with SI base units $\text{kg m}^2 \text{s}^{-3} \text{A}^{-1}$, so they match.

B.explanation: Both are force per unit area, $p = F/A$ and stress $= F/A$, in pascals with the same SI base units.

C.explanation: Spring constant is force per extension in $\text{N m}^{-1}$ while moment of a force is force times distance in $\text{N m}$, so base units differ.

D.explanation: Both have units of newton-metre, $\text{kg m}^2 \text{s}^{-2}$, torque as $F \times d$ and work as $F \times s$, so they match.
